title: Hub Attendant
leads: Nobody. You look after every phone in the hub, from the first bag to the morning pickup.
where: Inside the upload hub at the Central Cairo warehouse
hours: Nights. From the first bag in the evening to the morning pickup, before 7:00 AM
summary: You run one upload hub overnight: count, dock, upload, charge, log, and hand back every phone empty.

posting.headline: Hub attendant (night shift), Cairo
posting.about: KMSC runs the field operations behind one of the most ambitious artificial intelligence projects in the region, at factories, warehouses, and farms across Cairo. Every night the kit from every site comes to a hub and goes back charged and ready for the morning shift. You run one hub through the night, reporting to the Planning and Logistics Lead.
do: Work nights, from the first bag in the evening to the morning pickup before 7:00 AM.
Count every bag with the runner against its device list, and both of you sign.
Put every device on charge and check that each one is in the log.
Walk the racks every hour and replug any device that has stopped.
In the morning, repack the ready devices by site, count them with the runner, and sign the new list.
Send the Planning and Logistics Lead the night's numbers before 7:00 AM: devices in, out, and held.
need: 18 years or older, with a national ID.
Able to work nights and stay alert until morning.
Careful with equipment and honest with numbers.
Able to read a dashboard and write a clear log.
plus: You have worked a night shift before.
You have set up a router before.
offer: A steady monthly wage, paid on time.
Paid training, with your manager next to you on your first night.
A clear job with a clear list, in a company that writes everything down.
A hub of your own to run, as we grow from hundreds of people to thousands.
posting.apply: Send your name, your age, your area, your phone number, and whether you can work nights in Central Cairo. We call you back within two working days to book your onboarding screening.

offer.heading: Offer of employment
paragraphs: We are pleased to offer you the position of Hub Attendant at KMSC. You will report to {manager}, the Planning and Logistics Lead.
Your start date is {start}. Your first night is paid training, worked with {manager}.

terms.label: Hours
terms.v: Nights, from the first bag to the morning pickup before 7:00 AM

terms.label: Pay
terms.v: {pay} per month, paid at the end of the month

conditions: A copy of your national ID that shows you are 18 or older.
Your signature on the consent form and the fraud briefing.
One account in your own name. Accounts are never shared.
Your first night, worked with {manager} and signed off.
expect: Every bag is counted against its phone list and signed by you and the runner.
No phone leaves the hub before the dashboard shows it empty.
Only you and the runner touch the phones. A phone that goes home ends the job.
offer.closing: Please sign below to accept this offer. We look forward to working with you.

handbook.purpose: The client pays only for footage that reaches them. Every night the phones come to your hub. By 7:00 AM each one must be back at its site, empty and charged. Every count, every cable, and every log line is yours.
outcomes: Every bag counted against its phone list and signed by two people.
Every phone leaves empty and charged, or stays and its Portfolio Manager knows.
The Planning and Logistics Lead has the night's three numbers before 7:00 AM.
daily: Evening. Cables free, router on, dashboard open, log dated.
Each bag. Count by device number with the runner. Both sign. Wrong number: call the Planning and Logistics Lead now.
Then. Dock every phone, one per cable. Check the storage. Watch until all show uploading.
Every hour. Walk the racks. Replug a stopped phone. Still stuck: log it.
10:00 PM. Every run on the plan is in, or the Planning and Logistics Lead knows which is not.
Before the runner comes. Check the dashboard. A few videos left is fine. A full phone stays.
Early morning. Repack by site, new phone list, count with the runner, both sign.
Before 7:00 AM. Send the Planning and Logistics Lead phones in, phones out, phones held and why. Lock up.
By 8:00 PM the night before. Tell the Planning and Logistics Lead about any absence. The hub is covered from there.
weekly: Thursday, 4:00 PM. Confirm the tag of every held phone for the weekly count.
Thursday night. The full flush: every site's phones come in.
monthly: Go through the month's log with the Planning and Logistics Lead. Agree on what to change.
standards: Count by device number. Sign only the real count.
One phone per cable. Storage checked on every phone you dock.
A phone leaves empty or not at all.
Only you and the runner touch the phones.
One attendant per hub per night. A second when the hub takes more than 150 phones a night.
The Planning and Logistics Lead owns the hub line and the gear. Ask first.
never: Never send a phone back with videos still on it.
Never upload from anyone's home to get around a dead line.
A phone that goes home with you ends the job.
Saying the client's name to anyone outside the company ends the job.

firstMonth.what: The Planning and Logistics Lead works it with you. You do every count and log line, and get signed off.
You run the hub alone. The Planning and Logistics Lead reads your log and signed lists every morning.
No phone leaves full, no count is off, and the Planning and Logistics Lead has your numbers before 7:00 AM.

measures: Counts that matched the phone list, every night.
Phones that left the hub full: zero.
Phones stuck for more than an hour, per week.
Three numbers to the Planning and Logistics Lead before 7:00 AM, every day.
handbook.call: The Planning and Logistics Lead, now, for the line, the router, the gear, a run, a runner, or a count. Line down: restart the router once, then call. The runs go to the backup upload place the Planning and Logistics Lead names. An injury or the police: Moharam.
